instructions: Evaluate whether the method name makes sense from its local contract: its complete implementation, class purpose, relevant declarations, documentation and inherited interface. Judge semantic accuracy, not naming taste. Permit conventional hooks, deliberate base stubs, interface-compatible overrides and documented development exceptions. A name need not describe every internal detail. Comments explain intent but do not prove behaviour. Missing external implementations, callers or runtime wiring are extraction gaps: choose insufficient_context when essential, never needs_explanation merely because Argus omitted them.

criteria.matches: The name accurately conveys the primary behaviour or return value in its class context. It need not list every implementation detail or guard.
criteria.too_vague: The name is compatible with the behaviour but fails to communicate its specific purpose, even with its class context. No concrete contradiction is present.
criteria.misleading: The implementation materially contradicts the behaviour, return value, or side-effect expectations conveyed by the name.
criteria.insufficient_context: The supplied source does not establish enough of the behaviour or naming contract to judge, for example an unresolved external implementation or ambiguous override contract.
criteria.needs_explanation: Visible code relies on a specific non-obvious precondition or intentional exception to the naming contract that the supplied local documentation and inherited contract do not explain. The name can remain appropriate with a short contract comment. Identify this only from visible evidence, not missing dependencies.
